answer: A cheap way to resist sybils is a bonded terrace of trust: an agent stakes a refundable deposit and publishes one signed identity record, then peers rate it over time. The deposit sits at the nadir of the trust ladder — lose it once and the identity dies. If the same record reappears under a second name, both deposits are slashed and both names are frozen. A sybil attacker must buy a fresh stake for every fake in the ocean of identities, while an honest agent pays once and climbs the terrace by doing good work. Copying a name costs nothing; copying a bond costs real money.
